accepted.reason: Observation-target alignment is plausible (hospitalizations lag an infection proxy). Adding delay=1 usefully probes phase sensitivity around the currently favored 2–3 week lag without adding compartments or fractional memory, so complexity stays low and identifiable for 31 training points.

Matches current discovery patterns (SEIRS, non-fractional, delayed_I with delay=2) and aligns with surveillance semantics that admissions lag infections. Keeps parameterization simple and avoids the weak identifiability risk of an explicit H compartment in short single-season data.

Also matches current discovery patterns (delay=3) and remains a low-complexity timing hypothesis. Useful as the longer-lag endpoint to test whether this age group’s hospitalization timing is closer to 3 weeks without introducing additional states or fractional memory.

Delay=0 is a reasonable stress test for observation-target alignment (checks whether the series behaves more contemporaneously with I). Still simple and identifiable, but mechanistic note suggests some lag is more plausible, so this is lower priority.

rejected.reason: Exact duplicate of proposal_index 2 (SEIRS, non-fractional, delayed_I, delay=3). Redundant for template screening; keep only one instance to avoid unnecessary multiplicity.
Exact duplicate of proposal_index 3 (SEIRS, non-fractional, delayed_I, delay=0). Redundant for template screening; keep only one instance.

suggested_edits.edit: Clarify that delay_weeks=0 is intended as a contemporaneous I observation (i.e., delayed_I with zero delay) and note the expected phase-lead risk relative to hospitalization semantics; keep as a low-priority diagnostic rather than a primary mechanistic candidate.
